subject: Sampling from adjusted INLA model using inla.hyperpar()

messages.author: 2d2a4f5aa0df3ec7
messages.subject: Sampling from adjusted INLA model using inla.hyperpar()
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to improve the INLA estimation for the hierarchical model variance(the hyperparameters) using inla.hyperpar() because these approximations exhibited a multi-modal behaviour. And I think by decreasing the arguments dz(exploration step length) and increasing the log density difference threshold, it will help to smooth the distribution.

The original model is just a regular binary logistic regression and when I set dz as 0.5 and diff.logdens as 20, it seemed to work fine. But when I want to further finer the approximation by setting dz as 0.45 and diff.logdens as 25, the program crashed. 

I am wondering if anyone has tried to adjust the inla models using this function and what is the furthest that it took you. And if you have run into the similar issue, how did you end up fixing it?

Thank you guys in advance for your time and help. I really appreciate it!


Best regards,
Jocelyn

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sampling from adjusted INLA model using inla.hyperpar()
parts:
I guess you'll run of out memory as the number of combinations in the
hyper-param integration becomes large.

Multimodal behaviour in hyperpar is a hard one, unless you know where
the modes are.

you may try to define the integration scheme yourself, see 'int-design'
